turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“I’m here for my annual well-check, but I’ve noticed a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like patch on the back of my left hand. It doesn’t hurt and there’s no tenderness.”

“No, I wouldn’t say I’m experiencing actinic keratosis specifically—I’m just aware of that rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand. It hasn’t been painful or tender, and I haven’t noticed any other symptoms.”
[ASK] Do you have a fever or productive cough (coughing up phlegm) that suggests an acute lung infection?
“No, I don’t have a fever or a productive cough, and my review of systems is otherwise unremarkable. I’m only concerned about that rough, scaly patch on the back of my left hand.”

“No, I’m not experiencing vitiligo—nothing like widespread white patches or loss of skin color elsewhere. It’s only that single rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand, and it’s not painful or tender.”

“No, I’m not experiencing any joint pain, stiffness, or swelling that would suggest psoriatic arthritis. My main issue is still just the rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand, with no tenderness or pain.”

“I’m not sure it’s actinic keratosis, but the lesion is a single rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand. It hasn’t been tender or painful, and I haven’t noticed any other symptoms.”

“I’m not sure I can name it exactly, but I do have a single rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand, and it’s not painful or tender. I haven’t noticed any other symptoms, and I haven’t had fever or cough.”
